text:
eva_support: Customer reports: EU users intermittently hit us-west and see +250-500ms latency, some requests returning 401. They also noticed extra egress/billing due to cross-region failover. Sending logs they collected.

jin_eng: Can you paste one raw request/response from their logs? Specifically headers. Also which model/route? Any correlation ids?

eva_support: From customer (redacted):

```
> curl -v -H "Host: api.redwood.ai" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
< HTTP/2 401
< x-served-region: us-west-2
< x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 320
< x-request-id: req_abc123
{"error":"unauthorized","message":"invalid issuer"}
```

Notes: They always set X-Client-Region to eu-west-1. When routed correctly we'd expect x-served-region: eu-west-1 and ~40ms upstream time.

fleet_sre: We rolled out the region-fallback envoy filter ~6h ago to prefer healthy pools. Canary is 20%. I'm seeing healthcheck flaps on eu-edge (timeouts) causing fallback to default backend in us-west. Might explain cross-region routing.

ops_oncall: Grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/edge/route_errors shows spike starting 2026-03-15T09:12Z. Error tag: route_fallback_to_default. API error rate up ~1.8%. :warning:

jin_eng: Two things to check:
1) Route header matcher: our L7 config expects header `x-region` but customer sends `x-client-region`. If header is not matched, route falls through to default cluster.
2) Envoy header rewrite/strip: some routes do prefix_rewrite/host_rewrite which can drop downstream headers if the filter chain is misordered.

Example problematic snippet I found in canary config:
```
route:
  match:
    prefix: "/v1"
    headers:
      - name: "x-region"
        exact_match: "eu-west-1"
  route:
    cluster: "eu-pool"
    host_rewrite: "eu-proxy"
```
Customer uses `x-client-region`, so match fails and falls back.

mohammad_security: The 401s line up with JWT issuer checks. Our jwt-filter queries jwks proxied through regional auth. If request hits us-west, it fetches issuer config for us-west and the token iss doesn't match -> 401. So routing bug cascades to auth failure.

jin_eng: Repro steps for engineers:
1) curl with X-Client-Region: eu-west-1 -> observe x-served-region: us-west-2 (bad)
2) curl with X-Region: eu-west-1 -> observe x-served-region: eu-west-1 (good)
3) Toggle canary to 0% -> problem disappears.

Temporary mitigation: add a header translation rule in the gateway to copy `x-client-region` -> `x-region` for upstream routing, and roll back the canary. Long-term: fix route header match to accept both header names and ensure header preservation after rewrites.

redwood-deploy-bot: Deploy 5872 started: rollback region-fallback Canary -> target 0% (user: fleet_sre)

eva_support: I'll update the customer: short-term rollback + add header-copy. They requested refund for extra egress; please advise finance. Thanks.

fleet_sre: Opening incident INC-2026-0345, will track rollback, header-fix PR, and billing follow-up. I'll post updates here. :white_check_mark:
